title: Warren Buffett stands by comments that he supports outgoing Wells Fargo CEO
description: Berkshire Hathaway's Warren Buffett sits down with CNBC's Becky Quick in Grapevine Texas at an event for Hand-up Success. The two discuss whether Buffett supported Wells Fargo CEO Tim Sloan, hours before news broke about his retirement.  » Subscribe to CNBC: http://cnb.cx/SubscribeCNBC   About CNBC: From 'Wall Street' to 'Main Street' to award winning original documentaries and Reality TV series, CNBC has you covered. asr.full_text: Just hours before this news broke yesterday I actually spoke to Warren Buffett, who is Wells Fargo's largest shareholder. I asked him about Tim Sloan, and here's what he said when I asked him if Sloan had his support. Yet 100% I don't want his job. I actually came in once 28 years ago you know Solomon which, where the whole world was mad at him. And a — when I went to bed at night, I mean, I-I was scared because I didn't know what additionally had been done, you know, on 10 years earlier, or 5 years earlier. And, and how I deal with it, because people were furious with us. So I'm very empathetic to anybody that walks into a a big problem at a very very very large and politically sensitive, politically sensitive institution, where you've got maybe 250 or so thousand people and the bad acts in one of them you know couldn't reflect on you. Alright I spoke with Warren Buffett last night after all have lost a lot about himself that I think we can see it and the power of people and the bad acts of one of them can reflect on you. All right, I spoke with Warren buffett last night after all this happened, getting on a flight to come back to Dallas and by the time I landed around 830 I was able to touch with him, he said he knew about Tim sloan's departure day before on Wednesday. He couldn't say anything because it was before the news had been announced. He said he stands by his comments from yesterday that Tim Sloan does have his full support and also that he doesn't want his job. It's a very tricky situation. A lot of times when you get into these situations there's much more pressure than anybody anticipates than Tim might have anticipated or than Buffett had anticipated, too. But he says he stands by his support of Sloan in this entire situation. I guess Tim called it, I think we'll see the report on the Do not know what's coming
